KEY MESSAGE 1... 
A cold front associated with low pressure over southeast Quebec
is catching up to a warm front over central NY and PA early 
this afternoon, as a secondary low moves across southeast New 
England. A moist and humid air mass will briefly impact the 
region with dewpoints in the 60s to lower 70s this afternoon. 
An occluded front will bring some scattered showers and isolated
to scattered thunderstorms. PWATS have risen into the 1.5-2.0" 
range across the forecast area based on the SPC RAP 
Mesoanalysis, as the 12Z KALY sounding was 1.94". Low-level 
stratus is slowly eroding to partly to mostly cloudy conditions 
this afternoon. SBCAPE has had trouble developing from the 
Hudson River Valley/I-87 eastward so far. SBCAPEs 500-1000 J/kg
have been materializing north and west over the southwest
Adirondacks. The latest HREFs has mean SBCAPES of 750-1250 J/kg
late this afternoon into this evening from southern VT, the 
Capital Region, and the eastern Catskills south and east with 
weak deep shear 15-25 KT. The best 0-6 km bulk shear 25-35 KT is
over the far northwest zones, where some showers and isolated 
thunderstorms are developing over the western Adirondacks. The 
lack of robust instability, deep shear over the majority the 
forecast area, and weak lapse rates aloft should keep the 
thunderstorms that form non-severe. Some gusty winds and brief 
localized downpours could produce ponding of water with a few
storms. 

The front will move across the region slowly tonight with the 
abundant low-level moisture remaining in place, as widespread 
patchy fog to localized areas of dense fog will likely form, 
especially where rain occurs. Lows fall back into the mid 50s to
mid 60s with the coolest readings west of the Hudson River 
Valley over the higher terrain. Some modest cold advection will
occur over the northwest zones late.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

A few lingering showers persist over southern VT in the 
morning, as high pressure builds in across the region with 
partly to mostly sunny conditions and seasonable temps. High 
will be seasonable in the the 80-85F range in the valleys and 
mainly 70s over the hills and mtns. A window of mostly clear 
skies and light to calm winds will allow for some patchy 
radiational valley mist/fog in the sheltered valleys, as lows 
will be in the 50s around 60F. The frontal boundary approaches 
for Wed with a slight to low chance of showers and thunderstorms
especially north and west of the Capital Region over the 
western Dacks and west-central Mohawk Valley. Instability looks 
weak or limited with west-southwest low to mid-level flow. The 
front looks to weaken at night with the showers/thunderstorms 
diminishing. Temps will run near or slightly above seasonal 
normals with 70s to lower/mid 80s. The frontal boundary makes 
slow progress across the region by Thu morning. The best chance 
for isolated to scattered thunderstorms will be along and 
southeast of southern VT, the Greater Capital Region, and the 
eastern Catskills in the afternoon. A few thunderstorms could 
become strong, if moderate instability increases, but that is 
unclear at this this time with the medium range guidance/ensembles.

KEY MESSAGE 3...

Some uncertainty continues Fri into the weekend. Some of the
medium range guidance has a wave developing along the stalled 
front to the south of the region over PA and NJ for some rain to
impact locations from the Capital Region south and east, while 
the ECMWF and some ensembles keep it dry with high pressure 
building in. Our latest forecast from WPC for Days 4-7 keeps it
dry outside a slight chance of showers closer to I-84 on Fri. 
The deterministic, AI and ensemble guidance continues to forecast
a broad, deepening mid and upper level trough over southeast 
Canada, the Great Lakes Region and the Northeast for the 
upcoming weekend into early next week. The chances of showers 
and few thunderstorms continue late Sat into Sun for the trough 
and a potential closed low. Some locally heavy rain could occur 
depending where the mid and upper level low track and any 
surface cyclones, but timing, evolution details and the amount 
of rainfall still look very uncertain at this time. We will 
continue to closely monitor trends through the week, as this 
storm system is still several days away. Temps trend slightly 
cooler than normal.
